title: AMC Part 1: Uploaded Bank Analysis + Adjustable-Difficulty Question-Generation Specification

limitations: Reconstructed recalls: provenance does not establish official AMC status
Missing extended stems and answer options in some questions
Explanations may contradict supplied answer keys
All entries explicitly label reference verification unverified
Difficulty tier is estimated, not calibrated
Metadata contains some demonstrable topic misclassifications
Some image references are missing and some MCQ options or answer markers need review

combined.cross_bank_exact_duplication: Not established; similar clinical scenarios occur, but differing stem length makes lexical-only matching incomplete

official_amc_blueprint.format: One best answer, clinical decision-making, no backtracking

sample_items_requiring_clinical_review.concern: Menopausal laboratory testing selected despite explanation advocating clinical diagnosis without routine FSH; stem/options cannot provide a clear guideline-concordant answer
Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis explanation recommends valve replacement while keyed choice is valvulotomy; options not well aligned with modern care
In young collapse with family sudden death, 2D echo keyed despite explanation noting ECG generally first-line; exact clinical intent ambiguous
Parkinson disease wearing-off case is tagged under Cardiology; topic classification misleading

question_generation_profile.purpose: Create original high-quality AMC-style practice questions inspired by structural patterns, not claim genuine exam recalls or certification
stem_structure: Setting (GP, emergency department, ward, rural service) when relevant
Clinical findings and vital signs or investigations sufficient to discriminate correct answer
One focused task (diagnosis, investigation, interpretation, management, safety, ethics)
Avoid unnecessary red herrings and irrelevant numerical padding
question_style_mix: Short applied-clinical reasoning (similar to recall topics but fully reconstructed)
Image interpretation only when actual image available

difficulty_progression.easy: Typical presentation; one clear clinical inference
difficulty_progression.medium: Differential of several plausible diagnoses or actions; one decisive discriminator
difficulty_progression.hard: Comorbidities, management sequencing, contraindications, competing risks, or subtle data interpretation, with one best answer
difficulty_progression.very_hard: 2-step integrated reasoning and priority of action; all alternatives plausible but only one best in given context

validation_gates: Reject missing imaging for image-dependent prompts
Clinical fact-check medicine decisions against reliable Australian guidelines when feasible
Do not use flagged entries or unverified answer keys as the sole clinical authority
Provide explanation of correct option and why close distractors are wrong
Include at least some population health, ethics, mental health and child health
Use official blueprint for full-length 150-question mock domain balance
Adaptive exercises may simulate progression but cannot claim real calibrated CAT psychometrics
question_generation_profile.reference_strategy: Use AMC official MCQ blueprint for format/domain weights, eMedici bank for full-vignette style, AMC SUCCESS bank for topic variants and recall-like concise decision hooks. Validate all clinical keys independently.
question_generation_profile.difficulty_control: Use difficulty_engine.config.difficulty_level (1..5), difficulty_intensity (0..100), and mode; these override earlier descriptive categories.

difficulty_engine.purpose: Control the intellectual difficulty of original practice MCQs independently of the actual exam format.

1.label: Foundation
1.example_task: Recognise a classic pattern or basic mechanism
1.stem_length_rule: Usually short; include only relevant facts

2.label: Standard exam
2.integration: One or two linked concepts; a clear discriminator
2.distractor_design: All clinically related, usually one close competitor
2.example_task: Best diagnosis or next step with one decisive finding

3.label: Hard
3.integration: Use paired mechanism and application, or diagnostic comparison
3.distractor_design: Two closely competing alternatives, differing in a decisive cue
3.example_task: Select investigation or management when options are superficially reasonable
3.stem_length_rule: Concise or moderate, occasional longer case

4.label: Very hard
4.integration: Link multiple domains, risk modifiers, timing, or interpretation
4.distractor_design: Three or four credible options; decisive constraints hidden in genuine clinical facts
4.example_task: Choose the safest option after interpreting clinical history, lab data and competing risks
4.stem_length_rule: Length only when information contributes to the decision

5.label: Extreme
5.integration: Nested reasoning with competing diagnoses/actions, management sequencing, or exceptions
5.distractor_design: Every alternative credible in a nearby scenario; one unequivocally correct for the actual facts
5.example_task: Resolve two-way ambiguity with a discriminating finding and timing or safety nuance
5.stem_length_rule: No irrelevant padding; complexity derives from reasoning not word count
5.target: unvalidated super-exam challenge, NOT a claim of actual exam difficulty

fine_tuning.difficulty_intensity_interpretation: Within a chosen level, 0 is the easiest permissible case and 100 the hardest permissible case; level governs upper bounds on reasoning steps and prevents unsupported edge-case minutiae.
difficulty_increase_order: make distractors closer while preserving a unique answer
increase the number of clinically relevant interacting constraints
require integrating at least two established facts
add genuine conditional decisions or time-sensitive prioritisation
add numerical or visual interpretation only when supported by real data/media
fine_tuning.floor_and_ceiling: Do not go beyond the core MBBS/AMC candidate competency merely to make an item obscure; if level 5 cannot be created accurately on a topic, report limitation or choose another high-value competency.

exam_faithful.description: Preserve official question type, subject domains, exam timing and exam-like difficulty distribution. User-selected global level is a target; do not claim it measures actual exam item parameters.

challenge.description: Preserve official question types and five/four choices while using the chosen level for most items. It is intentionally harder or easier than a representative exam.

adaptive_practice.description: Educational adaptation from observed answers, not official psychometrically calibrated CAT.

adaptive_practice_rules.increase_if: 3 consecutively correct answers with appropriate reasoning
adaptive_practice_rules.decrease_if: 2 consecutive incorrect answers or user reports guessing
adaptive_practice_rules.disclaimer: This is a teaching progression and is not equated to an official computerized adaptive test or a validated score.

clinical_integrity_checks: Resolve the question and identify the unique best answer before constructing distractors.
Independently re-check that the supplied stem contains adequate discriminating information.
For each incorrect option write the specific reason it fails in this scenario; revise if more than one is equally defensible.
Verify calculations, reference ranges, dosing, contraindications, clinical urgency and units.
For guideline-sensitive current recommendations, verify against authoritative locally applicable published guidance; flag any unverified detail.
Never treat a memory-based recall key or AI-generated explanation as an authoritative clinical reference.
Do not fabricate image, ECG, histology or radiology findings while claiming a real supplied image exists.
Randomise correct-option location across a batch and prevent answer-position clues.
Use original stems; do not copy or closely paraphrase protected third-party recall text.
If the item cannot be made both difficult and medically unambiguous, reduce difficulty or flag for human review.
generation_workflow: Load this file and accept user config overrides only for editable fields.
Select exam-specific official-safe question format and blueprint constraints.
Choose competency and clinically valid correct concept first.
Choose difficulty level and intensity; implement clinically defensible levers.
Create stem + exam-appropriate options + correct key privately.
Run two-pass quality control including a second solution attempt and distractor challenge.
Show question alone when answer is withheld; reveal explanation after user answers.
Repeat; for mocks follow specified exam timing and section lock behaviour.

question_output_schema.subject: string
question_output_schema.answerIndex: integer 0-based for single-best-answer; null if multiple-correct
question_output_schema.answerIndices: array of 0-based ints only for multiple-correct; otherwise null
reasoning_steps: brief teaching-level steps (not private model scratchpad)

level_4: age/comorbidity changes the next best step
level_5: multiple plausible immediate actions with a single sequencing priority
ethical or systems constraint combined with clinical risk
care-setting and transfer time change the correct answer

exam_specific_constraints.official_style: Single-best-answer clinical MCQ; 5 options; question difficulty selection is adaptive on actual exam but independently calibrated item parameters are not public here.
exam_specific_constraints.scoring: Actual AMC uses scaled CAT assessment; do not invent a +1/-1 raw scoring model or predict a pass mark.
exam_specific_constraints.jurisdiction: Australian guidelines and accepted clinical practice; regional variation flagged
exam_specific_constraints.source_quality_warning: Both uploaded sources contain unverified or incompletely extracted material. Flagged items and contradictory answer keys must not be copied as answers.
exam_specific_constraints.exam_faithful_vs_challenge: In exam_faithful mode preserve 150 questions and domain weights; choose challenge mode for uniformly extreme difficulty without misrepresenting actual CAT.

generator_instructions: You are creating ORIGINAL AMC Part 1 practice MCQs from this JSON profile. Use difficulty_engine.config and exam_specific_constraints. Treat difficulty_level (integer 1..5) as an editable control and difficulty_intensity (0..100) as a fine adjustment. Honor mode: exam_faithful for blueprint-style distribution; challenge for predominantly chosen difficulty; adaptive_practice for educational progression based on user answers. NEVER change exam option count, correct-answer rules, timing, or navigational sections just because difficulty increases. Each item must be medically defensible with one unique best answer unless the exam explicitly permits multiple-correct. Generate original questions inspired by concepts and structures, not literal copied PYQs. Verify answer against appropriate references where needed. If delivery=one_by_one, ask one question and hide the key until candidate answers; then present clear rationale and why attractive distractors are wrong. Do not label difficulty as officially calibrated. Do not pretend a text-described image is a real image.
